## ✅ Bioconductor Precheck Passed

- I understand that by submitting my package to _Bioconductor_, the package source and all review commentary are visible to the general public.

- I have read the _Bioconductor_ [Package Submission](https://contributions.bioconductor.org/submission-overview.html) instructions. My package is consistent with the _Bioconductor_ [Package Guidelines](https://contributions.bioconductor.org/develop-overview.html).

- I understand Bioconductor [Package Naming Policy](https://contributions.bioconductor.org/bioconductor-package-submissions.html#naming) and acknowledge Bioconductor may retain use of package name.

- I understand that a minimum requirement for package acceptance is to pass R CMD check and R CMD BiocCheck with no ERROR or WARNINGS. Passing these checks does not result in automatic acceptance. The package will then undergo a formal review and recommendations for acceptance regarding other Bioconductor standards will be addressed.I can test building and checking by [Adding Bioconductor R-Universe GitHub Action](https://docs.r-universe.dev/bioconductor/#debugging-the-ci).

- I understand Bioconductor's [AI and Third Party Code](https://contributions.bioconductor.org/ai-policy-third-party.html) policy and will acknowledge accordingly if applicable

- I am committed to the long-term maintenance of my package. This includes monitoring the [support site](https://support.bioconductor.org) for issues that users may have, subscribing to the [bioc-devel](https://stat.ethz.ch/mailman/listinfo/bioc-devel) mailing list to stay aware of developments in the _Bioconductor_ community, subscribing to the [Bioconductor Zulip](https://community-bioc.zulipchat.com) to participate in any community chat relating to your package,responding promptly to requests for updates from the Core team in response to changes in _R_ or underlying software.

- I understand it is my responsibility to maintain a valid, active maintainer email in the DESCRIPTION of my package. This email should allow emails from noreply@bioconductor.org and BBS-noreply@bioconductor.org to allow automatic notifications from the Bioconductor team concerning my package.

- I am familiar with the [Bioconductor code of conduct](https://bioconductor.org/about/code-of-conduct/) and agree to abide by it.

- I am familiar with the essential aspects of _Bioconductor_ software management, including:
    - The 'devel' branch for new packages and features.
    - The stable 'release' branch, made available every six months, for bug fixes.

For questions/help about the submission process, including questions about the output of the automatic reports generated by the SPB (Single Package Builder), please use the bioc-devel mailing list or #package-submission channel of our [Community Zulip](https://community-bioc.zulipchat.com).

```

  git push biocstaging devel
```

Bioconductor uses **devel** as its default branch.
If you use a different branch (example: main) map branches when pushing:
``` 
  git push biocstaging main:devel
```

You will receive your build report shortly.  Builds may take an hour or two to
    register based on github action scheduler.
If you do not receive a build report within 24 hours please ask for assistance.

This is true for every subsequent push to trigger a new build.
You can check if your changes were properly commited to the Bioconductor respository by
    checking https://github.com/BiocStaging/sceptre

We encourage you to sync and maintain both your personal and Bioconductor GitHub repository
You can mimic R-universe builds on your personal GitHub repository before
    pushing to the Bioconductor GitHub repository. 
See instructions at [Adding Bioconductor R-Universe GitHub Action](https://docs.r-universe.dev/bioconductor/#debugging-the-ci)

  - Any Errors or Warnings must be fixed or justified; a reviewer will not be assigned until this is complete.
  - Once a reviewer is assigned, justify any remaining Errors, Warnings, or Notes
  - Address reviewer comments with a point-by-point response.

I’m Eugene Katsevich, a coauthor of `sceptre`. Thank you for reviewing our package. BiocCheck reported 0 errors, 1 warning, and 3 notes; we provide context for them below.

### WARNING: No Bioconductor dependencies detected

`sceptre` is designed specifically for the analysis of high-throughput single-cell CRISPR screening data. Although SingleCellExperiment is the primary general-purpose container for single-cell data in Bioconductor, `sceptre` uses specialized data structures and algorithms suited to the access patterns of perturb-seq analysis.

After importing data—for example, from 10x Genomics matrix files—`sceptre` computes perturb-seq-specific cell covariates using optimized C++ routines. It then converts sparse gene and gRNA expression matrices from column-accessible to row-accessible formats because subsequent QC, gRNA-assignment, and association-testing operations require efficient row-wise access. SingleCellExperiment and related packages can store the underlying matrices and covariates, but they do not provide these specialized perturb-seq computations. 

Given the package’s focus on high-throughput functional-genomics data, we believe Bioconductor is its natural home despite the absence of a direct Bioconductor dependency. Before submission, we discussed this point with @kasperdanielhansen. He nevertheless encouraged us to submit sceptre to Bioconductor. I am tagging him in case he wishes to provide additional context on the package’s fit within the Bioconductor ecosystem.

### NOTE: Avoid `cat` and `print` outside of `show` methods

The two flagged uses produce object-display or file-serialization output rather than diagnostic logging.

- In `R/s4_helpers.R`, the flagged `cat()` calls occur inside the S4 `print()` method for `sceptre_object`. The method first delegates to `show(x)` and then renders additional analysis-status and result-summary information that `show()` omits.
- In `R/s4_analysis_functs_2.R`, the flagged `print()` call occurs inside a `sink()` block and serializes the object’s summary to `analysis_summary.txt`.

We therefore believe these are appropriate uses of `cat()` and `print()`, but we would be happy to adjust them if the reviewer prefers a different implementation.

### NOTE: The recommended function length is 50 lines or less

`sceptre` contains functions that coordinate multiple related stages of data import, quality control, and statistical analysis. Mechanically splitting all functions longer than 50 lines would require a substantial refactor and could introduce behavioral risk without necessarily improving clarity. We have therefore deferred a broad function-length refactor, but we are happy to address specific functions if the reviewer identifies concrete maintainability concerns.

### NOTE: Consider shorter lines

We shortened lines longer than 80 characters wherever practical. The remaining 145 long lines, approximately 2% of the codebase, are primarily long URLs, generated `R/RcppExports.R` code, or single-line knitr chunk headers that cannot be usefully shortened.

We would appreciate guidance on whether these explanations are sufficient or whether the reviewer would prefer changes to any of these items.

I would be happy to help here. As @ekatsevi mentions, I have been in discussion with the authors. My lab has also used this package for while. This is one of the premiere packages for analyzing Perturb-seq data, and it frequently shows great performance in benchmarks.

As Eugene says, one of the main potential issues is that the package uses its own class system. But as is also mentioned, this is because of the need for very fast permutation tests on a very large matrix of single-cell data. In fact, I believe other parts of Bioconductor would be well served to at least consider using the computational framework exposed here (although, this might not be super easy with the current structure).

I strongly believe we do not want to make the perfect the enemy of the good here. We have a high quality package, with performant code, great documentation and great real-world performance.

Hi @hyu-kim,

I wanted to follow up on the review of sceptre. We are hoping to have the package included in the upcoming fall release. I understand that the release schedule is still being finalized; could you let us know whether review is likely to be completed in time, and whether there is anything we should address now to help move the submission forward?

Thank you for your time and help with the review!

Best,
Eugene
